comparison.text: Outdoor air pollution causes about 4.2 million early deaths a year worldwide, says WHO. It is one of the biggest killers nobody posts about.
comparison.source_name: WHO fact sheet, Ambient (outdoor) air quality and health (2019 estimate)
comparison.caveat: A modeled global estimate for 2019, the latest WHO headline figure, with uncertainty in the millions.

comparison.text: A NIOSH N95 removes at least 95 percent of airborne particles when it seals to your face. On days like this, it is not paranoia, it is arithmetic.
comparison.source_name: CDC NIOSH, Proper N95 Respirator Use (Science Bulletin)
comparison.caveat: The 95 percent is the certified filter performance with a proper seal. Beards, gaps and surgical masks do not deliver it.

comparison.text: Kids breathe faster than adults, so they absorb more of this per kilo. They also live closer to the ground, where some pollutants peak. WHO's words, not ours.
comparison.source_name: WHO, More than 90% of the world's children breathe toxic air every day (2018)
comparison.caveat: Direct WHO statements: children 'breathe more rapidly than adults and so absorb more pollutants' and 'live closer to the ground, where some pollutants reach peak concentrations'.

comparison.text: Plot twist: 68 percent of outdoor air pollution deaths are heart disease and stroke. It was never just about your lungs.
comparison.source_name: WHO fact sheet, Ambient (outdoor) air quality and health
comparison.caveat: WHO's breakdown of premature deaths linked to outdoor air pollution: 68 percent ischaemic heart disease and stroke, 14 percent COPD, 14 percent acute lower respiratory infection, 4 percent lung cancer.

comparison.text: Today's air is worse than 100 percent of days this season in Nashik. Ranked, logged, versioned.
comparison.caveat: Season means the trailing 90 days of this project's own observations. Small archive early on means noisy percentiles, and the repo shows exactly how small.
